paper.title_en: Regge bounds and eikonal estimates in scalar effective field theory
paper.abstract_en: Positivity bounds are derived from twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which hold only if the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partialφ)^4/Λ^4$ and $g_6(\partialφ)^6/Λ^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. Matching the two regions gives the phase-model growth $s^{8/7}$ for the quartic sector and $s^{16/15}$ for the sextic sector, while a transition scale fixed by the cutoff gives the conditional bound $s^{7/4}$; in the forward limit the same construction gives only the marginal growth $s^2$, so that Regge boundedness remains an assumption on the completion. Under this assumption the $2\to 2$ and $2\to 4$ absorptive parts below the cutoff restrict the couplings to $0<g_4\le 80π^2/7$ and $-7.2\times 10^5\lesssim g_6\lesssim 6.9\times 10^5$.
